doc.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Milt Shaw and the valet trick for a bath
summary: Booking agent Billy Shaw's son Milt toured with the band; Moody posed as his valet to get a bath in a Southern hotel.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: And -- and Milt Shaw [phonetic sp.] was the son of -- of -- of Shaw.

Billy Shaw, right. So Milt liked -- he liked Dizzy very much because he played trumpet. So, he was like the manager, so he -- his father sent him on the road with us. Me and Milt were the same age. All right? So we got -- when we got down South, I wanted a bath so bad, man, you know, and wanted to go, so I said, "Hey, Milt." I said, "You do me a favor?" He says, "Yeah, what?" I said, "Man, let me carry your bags and pretend like I'm your valet and let me 'cause I wanna get a bath, and I wanna go." He says, "Okay."

So I had his bags. "Hey, boy! Bring those over here!" I said, "Yessir." You know. [laughter] So I was, "Yessir" and I brought his bags and I got up in the room, put them down, I took me a bath, slept, had me a good night's sleep. And then brought his bags back downstairs, you know, that night and came out. That was it. [laughter] Yeah, you know.
